children: Wall Street's major averages ended mixed on Friday, with the Nasdaq leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year.
The benchmark S&P 500 gained 0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite finished advanced 1.1%, while the blue-chip Dow ended down 0.5%.
The S&P 500 Health Care Sector Index
gained 0.16% for the week.
The top S&P 500 healthcare gainers and losers for the past week are as follows:
Top five gainers:
IDEXX Laboratories
Moderna
Baxter International
Zimmer Biomet
Stryker
Top five losers:
Illumina
CVS Health
Charles River Laboratories International
Eli Lilly
Pfizer
Here are some of the important healthcare stories from this week:
Moderna rises as overseas COVID-19 vaccine sales drive Q3 beat, guidance hike
Moderna
shares
in premarket trading on Friday after the biotech delivered better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and lifted its full-year growth outlook, citing higher COVID-19 vaccine sales in

The Cambridge, Massachusetts-headquartered firm reported $1.3B in revenue for the quarter, with ~29% YoY growth beating the consensus by $409.8M, mainly due to improved COVID-19 vaccine sales in international markets.
Moderna

recorded $162M in net income for Q3 compared with a $200M loss in the prior-year period, beating the estimates by $1.63 per share as its R&D expenses dropped ~27% YoY to $583M, falling short of $750M in the consensus according to Bloomberg data.
Citing the ongoing momentum, Moderna

raised its full-year topline growth outlook to 15% - 25%, up from the 10% growth previously and exceeding ~8% YoY growth in the consensus. The company also revised its 2026 capital expenditure estimate to roughly $200M, down from $200M - $300M previously, and compared with $244M projected by analysts.
CVS Health nears a six-month low as breakup plans overshadow Q3 beat
CVS Health

more than 12% on Wednesday to hit the lowest level since early May despite consensus-beating Q3 2026 results after the healthcare giant announced plans to split into two independent publicly traded companies in 2028.

The transaction separating CVS' nationwide network of roughly 9,000 retail pharmacies from its Aetna health insurer and PBM unit CVS Caremark offset positives from a healthy Q3 beat and a guidance hike, according to analysts.

Leerink Partners analyst Michael Cherny, who has an Outperform rating on CVS, argued that the company's “a VERY strong 3Q print” also included an increased full-year outlook, but the spinoff announcement overshadowed it.

“So much of the focus shifts from fundamentals to the spin-off transaction, but at this point it is important to note that fundamentals, across both segments, remain quite strong," Bloomberg reported, quoting Cherny.
“The most important thing we can hope to hear is commentary on FY27, in particular re-framing the HSS headwinds," he wrote.
Pfizer hikes 2026 outlook despite flat Q3 revenue: names new CFO
After reporting better-than-expected Q3 2026 financials on Tuesday, Pfizer
hiked its full-year outlook even as its quarterly revenue remained relatively flat amid less demand for its COVID-19 products.
Concurrently, Pfizer
also appointed Cecile Guegan as its next chief financial officer and executive vice president, effective November 1, to replace former CFO Dave Denton, who left the company in August.
Guegan joined the New York-based pharma giant through its 2009 acquisition of Wyeth and most recently served as Senior Vice President of Finance for Pfizer’s
Global Biopharmaceuticals business.

For Q3, the company reported $16.6B in revenue, a decrease of $71M from the prior year quarter but exceeding the consensus by $700M. The company reported $0.87 of adjusted earnings per share, also unchanged from the prior year period but exceeding the consensus by $0.14.
Looking ahead, Pfizer
raised its full-year outlook for revenue and adjusted EPS to $62.0B to $64.0B and $2.95 - $3.05 from $60.5B - $62.5B and $2.80 - $3.00, in line with $62.2B and $2.96 in the consensus, respectively.
Novartis slips amid safety concerns tied to Zolgensma
Novartis

ADRs fell on Thursday after patient advocates highlighted safety concerns potentially linked to its gene therapy, Zolgensma, including nine cases of tumors found in children treated with the one-time therapy.

“SMA Europe is aware of information currently circulating regarding Zolgensma and reports of tumors in children who have previously received treatment,” a patient advocacy group said in a statement on Thursday.
The nonprofit urged Novartis

to share more information, noting that the cases “may be deeply concerning for families, particularly for parents whose children have already received Zolgensma or who are currently considering treatment.”

The Swiss drugmaker launched Zolgensma in 2019 after the FDA approved it for children aged less than two years with spinal muscular atrophy, a rare neuromuscular disease and a leading genetic cause of infant mortality.
In a statement to SMA Europe, Novartis

said that it is aware of nine cases of tumors diagnosed in Zolgensma-treated patients, including two cases where there is evidence to suggest that vector DNA of the gene therapy has been integrated into the DNA of the patients.
The Basel firm added that the Zolgensma prescribing information flags the risk of tumor formation due to vector integration.

“Patient safety is our priority. In each case, we timely and appropriately notified health authorities and will continue to work with them on next steps. We appreciate the opportunity to respond to community questions,” the company said.
